#### 3. 11b Energy consumption: change against scenario 1 (v0.3.14; legacy F7)

`echg` rows give the change against scenario 1 in the same year, in ktoe. The levels come from section 11:
- by fuel, from the fuel rows (power generation fuels included);
- by sector group, from the sector totals of sections 5-8;
- power generation fuel use;
- the total.

The change is read through helper row 10 (`INDEX(scenario 1 .. this column, position of scenario 1's year)`).

`epct` rows give the % change: `echg / (level - echg)`, and 0 when scenario 1 is 0.

Not as rows: the energy-balance matrix (legacy G; Q30). It is a rearrangement of section 11 and goes to an output sheet later.

#### 4. 13b CO2 change, grid emission intensity, Kaya identity (v0.3.14; legacy F13, row 6582, F14)

**CO2 change.** `cchg` gives the change of CO2 from fuel combustion against scenario 1, by fuel and by sector group, power included (MtCO2).

**Grid intensity.** `co2.grid` = CO2 of power generation x Million / (total generation in MWy x `HoursYr`), in tCO2 per MWh. Egypt: 0.41 in 2022 (legacy 0.38) and 0.33 in 2030.

**Kaya identity (legacy rows 18877-18893), as legacy (v0.3.18):**
- **GDP:** baseline real GDP (the header row), in every scenario.
- **CO2:** total CO2 including industrial processes (`ghg.g.co2`).
- **Energy:** total primary energy supply, `kaya.tpes` (legacy row 18880). It is the fuel use of section 11 (fuels burnt in power plants included, biomass included), plus primary electricity: the energy input `pe` of nuclear, wind, solar, hydro and other renewables in section 3. The input is generation divided by the type's efficiency (physical energy content method: nuclear at 38%, renewables at about 1). Egypt 2022: 89,471 ktoe = legacy 89,471. Energy intensity 163.57 ktoe per USD bn = legacy.

  v0.3.14-v0.3.17 used fuel use only (2.6% lower in 2022). This was corrected at the user's request (2026-10-16). Legacy's broken "simplified Kaya" row (18931, -97%) is a different row and is not used.

`kaya.*` levels:

| Row | Content | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| `kaya.pop` | Population | mn |
| `kaya.gpc` | GDP per capita | thousand USD |
| `kaya.tpes` | Total primary energy supply | ktoe |
| `kaya.ei` | Energy intensity | ktoe per USD bn |
| `kaya.ci` | Carbon intensity | ktCO2 per ktoe |

`kidx.*` indices against the base year of scenario 1: population, GDP, GDP per capita, energy intensity, carbon intensity, CO2. `kidx.chk` is the product of the four factors and equals the CO2 index exactly.

Egypt 2030:
- baseline: CO2 x1.17, with energy intensity 0.81 and carbon intensity 1.03;
- carbon tax: energy intensity 0.74, CO2 x1.10.

The efficiencies of wind (1.004), solar (1.026) and hydro (0.937) are legacy's power data, kept (issue I93).

Population is the prototype's UN series: 111.7 mn in 2022, against legacy's 103.6 mn (legacy bug L20, fixed). GDP per capita is therefore lower than in legacy, and the identity still holds.

LAMBDA `SAFEDIV` (amount / activity, 0 when the activity is 0) is used in the LAMBDA column.

#### 5. 14b GHG change and energy GHGs including forcing (v0.3.14; legacy F12)

**GHG change.** `gchg` gives the change against scenario 1 by inventory category (energy, industrial processes, agriculture, LULUCF, waste, other) and by gas (Mt CO2e).

**Broad sectors.** Legacy's "GHG by broad sector" (rows 18229-18243) is the inventory categories, which section 14 already has. No allocation of CH4 and N2O to sectors is needed (Q32).

**Energy GHGs with forcing.** `ghg.enrp` = energy GHGs + the forcing of the local pollutants (`apf.all`, section 15): legacy "Total GHGs and PM", rows 18310 and 18321.

**Later:** the NDC comparison (Q33; needs the NDC table).

#### 6. Section 17 Carbon pricing (v0.3.15; legacy F3, F5d-e)

**Implicit carbon price by fuel (`cpi.<fuel>`, USD per tCO2).** Revenue net of subsidies of the fuel, divided by its CO2:
- revenue: existing taxes + subsidies + new policies, final use (`rfu`) and power generation (`rfg`);
- CO2: from section 13.

This is legacy's "total carbon price" by fuel (F5d), which divides the tax-and-subsidy wedge per GJ by the emission factor. `cpi.all` is the same over the fossil fuels.

Biomass is left out (Q34): it has no CO2, and legacy gives `#DIV/0!`. Egypt 2022: gas -151, diesel -249, LPG -280, all fossil fuels -179 USD per tCO2 (subsidies). A carbon tax of 20 USD raises every fuel by about 20.

**Effective carbon rate (`ecr`, legacy row 16662).** `(rnet + rnew) / energy CO2`, as legacy, so VAT, the electricity subsidy gap and electricity VAT count (issue I36: the OECD rate counts carbon taxes, excises and permit prices only). Egypt 2022: -207 USD per tCO2 (legacy -122; the price data differ).

**Effective carbon tax (`cpeff`, legacy row 16137).** Carbon price x the share of energy CO2 it covers.

**Coverage.**
- `covct.<sector>`: CO2 covered by the new carbon tax in each of the 17 coverage sectors. It is the CO2 of the fuels whose switch is on (`fc` rows), counted only where the sector's carbon-tax rate is above 0. A sector in a non-complementary ETS has none. Power uses the CO2 of coal, gas and oil generation.
- `cov.ct.<group>`, `cov.ct.all`: shares of national energy CO2 (legacy rows 16152-16157). Egypt, carbon tax scenario, 2030: 99.8% (legacy 98.8%), of which power 41%.
- `cov.ets`: ETS coverage share (from `co2.ets`).
- `cov.all`: their sum.

The `cpi`, `ecr`, `cpeff` and coverage-share rows call `SAFEDIV` / `SCALEBY` in the LAMBDA column.

MTOutputs: `cpi.all.all`, `ecr.all.all`, `cpeff.all.all`, `cov.all.all.all`.

#### 7. 16b External balance (v0.3.16; legacy F11, data rows 741-743)

Section 16 is renamed "GDP effects and external balance" (Q39).

**Data.** Legacy Mitigation rows 741-743 give the energy trade balance (exports - imports, USD bn real) of gas, oil products and coal, with their share traded: gas 0.19, oil products 0.47, coal 1.0. They are extracted by `extract_gdp` into sheet WEO (`EGY|tb_<group>`, `EGY|ts_<group>`).

**Change in net imports (`xnim`, USD bn real; Q37).** By fossil fuel: change in use (11b, `echg`) x PJ per ktoe x supply price (section 2, `sp`, \$/GJ) x the share traded of the fuel's group (column D) / MperBn. Prices used:
- coal and gas: the industry supply price;
- jet fuel: kerosene;
- other fuels: their own `.all` price code.

The rows are summed by group (oil, gas, coal) and in total. Egypt, carbon tax 20 USD, 2030: -1.2 bn USD (oil -0.93).

Legacy leaves the share out for oil (bug L49, fixed), so its oil effect is about twice as large.

**Trade balance.**
- `xtb.<group>`, `xtb.all`: the baseline energy trade balance (data). Egypt 2022: -6.7 bn USD.
- `xtbp`: the scenario's balance, `xtb.all - xnim.all`.
- `xtb.pct`, `xnim.pct`: shares of baseline real GDP (`SAFEDIV`).

Legacy's balance-of-payments panel (rows 18195-18219) is not replicated (bug L50):
- its pre-policy current account is `#NAME?`;
- its rows lag one column, so it shows the 2021 balance (-5.85) in 2022;
- the sign of its policy net imports looks reversed.

The current-account level (WEO `BCA`, Q38) waits for WEO data in the data step.

MTOutputs: `xnim.all.all`, `xtbp.all.all`, `xtb.pct.all.all`.

#### 8. Section 18 Welfare and externalities, climate part (v0.3.17; legacy F10, rows 17392-17742)

**Settings (rows 32-42; legacy rows 17671-17677).** Defaults as legacy:

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| Target-consistent price `SCCTgt` | 75 USD per tCO2 real |
| Its year `SCCTgtYr` | 2030 |
| Real growth `SCCGr` | 4% a year |
| National and global SCC source (`NSCCSrc`, `GSCCSrc`) | Target. The choices are Target, Ricke, Manual, EPA |
| Ricke et al. (2018) settings | pure rate of time preference 2, elasticity 1p5 |
| US EPA SCC in the base year | 62 |

**SCC options (Q40; legacy rows 17680-17713).** Egypt 2022 values are given.

| Option | Formula | Egypt 2022 |
|---|---|---|
| `scc.tgt` | SCCTgt x (1 + SCCGr)^(year - SCCTgtYr) | 54.8 |
| `scc.rkn` | Ricke national value (new data sheet `SCC`, key `egy.2.1p5`) x (1 + SCCGr)^(year - base year) | 6.87 |
| `scc.rkg` | Ricke global value (`wld.2.1p5`), same growth | 462 |
| `scc.man` | manual path: 'Manual inputs' row 237 (v0.5.2, L103 fixed; legacy reads the path typed on Mitigation row 17683) | 50.0 in 2025, +4% a year |
| `scc.epa` | US EPA value, same growth | 62 |
| `scc.nat`, `scc.glo` | the selected options (CHOOSE) | |

All equal legacy.

**Climate damages.**
- `dmg`: SCC x GHG excl. LULUCF (section 14), USD bn. Egypt 2022: 22.9 bn, against legacy's 22.0, because the inventories differ slightly.
- `wcli`: damages of scenario 1 - damages of the scenario, i.e. the damages avoided (national, global).

**Efficiency (deadweight) costs of energy (Q41; legacy rows 17636-17648).** For each fuel, power generation fuels included, and electricity:
- tax wedge `wdg` = revenue net of subsidies per unit of use (USD m per ktoe; 12d rows / section 11 use; electricity: `rfu.ecy` / electricity demand);
- cost `eff` = -(wedge + wedge of scenario 1) / 2 x change in use / MperBn (LAMBDA TRAPEZOID).

This is legacy's trapezoid: Harberger triangle + rectangle. With subsidies (negative wedges), a fall in use is a gain. Egypt, carbon tax 20 USD, 2031: -1.25 bn USD (gain), mostly electricity and diesel.

Legacy bugs not replicated:
- the LPG pre-existing tax row is empty (the LPG average tax is halved);
- diesel and kerosene are converted with the wrong factors;
- the coal row is offset;
- non-road oil is `#N/A`.

**Efficiency costs of the methane fee (Q43; legacy rows 17628-17634, "integral").** For each methane source:
- `mfp`: the fee per t CH4 used on the abatement curve, capped where abatement reaches 1 (MFEEPRICE);
- `mfc`: the area under the abatement curve, a x fee^b, i.e. unabated emissions x abated share x price x b / (1 + b) / Million (MFEECOST).

The fee is 0 in the shipped scenarios. A test with a fee of 50 USD per tCO2e agrees with the Python recomputation.

**Welfare summary (national; legacy rows 17727-17742).**
- `wel.usd` = avoided national damages - efficiency costs of energy - methane-fee costs;
- `wel.pct`, `wel.cli`, `wel.eff`: shares of baseline real GDP.

Egypt, carbon tax 20 USD, 2031: +3.2 bn USD (0.39% of GDP).

**Not as rows (Q42, NORMS 3c):** the air-pollution and transport co-benefits, externalities per unit, explicit and implicit subsidies, efficient prices. They come with their modules.

MTOutputs: `scc.all.nat`, `wcli.all.nat`, `eff.all.all`, `mfc.all.all`, `wel.all.usd`, `wel.all.pct`.


### Multiple scenarios: definitions, batch run, stored results, comparison

Equations: `Equations.md`; workbook formulas: `Formulas.md`.

The model calculates two scenarios at a time: the baseline and one live policy scenario. A batch macro copies each scenario definition into the live scenario, calculates it and stores its results as values, which are compared afterwards. This follows legacy CPAT, where a macro copies each scenario column into the column used for calculation and stores the outputs.

#### 1. Where things are

| Place | What it holds |
|---|---|
| ScenarioDefinition, scenario 1 | The **baseline**, stored once. |
| ScenarioDefinition, scenario 2 | The **live policy scenario**. The batch run overwrites it with each definition and restores it at the end. |
| ScenarioDefinition, columns to the right | **Scenario definitions**, one full ScenarioDefinition column each: short name (row 2, the legend in the charts), Run? (Yes/No), number (previous + 1), name, then the inputs. Red cells differ from the template. To add one, copy the last definition one column to the right and edit it. Blank columns are grouped and collapsed. |
| Mitigation, Distribution | Two scenario groups: 1 = the baseline (plain formulas), 2 = the live scenario (every calculated cell calls its named LAMBDA). More live scenarios: copy group 2 to the right and set its scenario number; MTOutputs has room for 12 scenario blocks. |
| MTOutputs | The results of every scenario group in the **legacy MTOutputs layout** (v1.0.4): columns A Include?, B Country, C Scenario, D CPATIndicator, E CPATCode (our code, from Country, Tab, Variable, SubScenario), F the legacy CPAT code, G Tab, H Variable, I Unit, J SubScenario, years K:AD (distribution rows: deciles 1-10 in K:T); legacy's sections and rows in legacy order, one block per scenario; a row legacy lists and the prototype does not have stays with Include? = No and the reason (helper columns right of the years: lookups, legacy code body and row, match). Found on Mitigation and Distribution by output code. |
| StoredOutputs | Results as **values only**: the MTOutputs indicators of each scenario, under its ID and output code (country.stem.ID). ID 1 is the baseline; a definition keeps its ScenarioDefinition number. Sorted by indicator, then ID (like variables together); every lookup matches the output code, so any order works. |
| ScenarioCompare | The **dashboard** and every user entry of the front: results from Live (MTOutputs) or Stored (StoredOutputs), the year, the data source of the linked tables. Core buttons (green) and the others (grey); key results for one year of up to 10 scenarios against the baseline; a bar chart; time series with their chart beside them. |
| VBA module CPATScenarios | The macros below. The workbook is an .xlsm; the source is also in `CPATScenarios.bas`. |
| MacroCheck | Report of the first-run test macro CheckBatchRun. |

#### 2. Shipped definitions

| No. | Name | Inputs changed from the template |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Carbon price \$20/tCO2 from 2027 | The live scenario's settings |
| 4 | Package A: carbon tax to \$50 by 2030 + feebates (transport, industry) | Carbon tax \$10 (2027) to \$50 (2030). Feebates 2027-2030: transport \$10 → \$50, industry \$5 → \$25. Feebate coverage adds road, mining & chemicals, and iron & steel |
| 5 | Package B: ETS on power and industry + carbon tax \$25 elsewhere | Carbon tax \$25 from 2027. New ETS from 2027: cap −5% (2027) to −20% (2035) of baseline covered emissions, constant afterwards. Template ETS coverage (power, mining & chemicals, iron & steel, non-ferrous metals, cement), default benchmarks and volatility |

Paths continue after their target year as set in the model: the carbon price follows its ScenarioDefinition switch, and feebates continue linearly.

#### 2b. Main scenario choice and regulations as shadow prices (v0.4.16, LD9)

ScenarioDefinition row 13 (`ScenarioSelected`, " - Carbon tax" in every shipped scenario) picks a row of the legacy scenario table (legacy Mitigation rows 222-262, columns N:AC; sheet Mapping, block "Main scenarios"): whether the scenario prices carbon explicitly (legacy row 259), its efficiency adjustment (ScenarioDefinition rows 247-251) and the sectors its shadow price covers (rows 240-257).

- Explicit scenarios (carbon tax, total carbon price, coal excise, road fuel tax, electricity emissions tax and excise): the carbon price path of ScenarioDefinition rows 18-21 is the carbon tax (`cpx` = `cptraj`), as before.
- Shadow-pricing scenarios (feebates, power supply feebates, energy efficiency regulations, power feebate, vehicle fuel economy, residential and industrial efficiency regulations; and "Baseline"): no explicit carbon tax (`cpx` = 0); the carbon price path becomes a shadow price on the efficiency margin, `reg.<sector>` = `cp.shd` x the scenario's adjustment (energy efficiency 247, vehicle fuel economy 248, residential 249, industrial 250, feebates 251; Egypt 0.7, feebates 1) x 1 if the scenario covers the sector. It enters `shpx` (with the feebate part, now x row 251, and the ETS benchmark part), so fuel use responds through efficiency only, and power through `shk` (legacy bugs L87, L88 fixed: legacy's regulation share is 0 and never reaches power).
- The road vehicle feebate of the engineer road model adds `reg.rod` (the road regulation shadow price) instead of the carbon price, which is in the fuel price already (prototype bug M13).
- A text that is not in the table counts as explicit pricing (as the shipped " - Carbon tax").

#### 3. Macros

Core buttons (green, on ScenarioCompare): **Recalculate now**, **Recalculation on/off**, **Run stored scenarios**, **Update data tables**. The others are grey, below them.

- **RunAllScenarios** (button Run stored scenarios): stores the baseline under ID 1 if none is stored yet. Then, for every definition with Run? = Yes, it copies the definition's inputs and name into the live scenario (skipping two formula rows), clears the ETS price override and recalculates, runs the ETS goal seek if the definition applies a new ETS without "Override ETS price" = Yes, and stores the live scenario's outputs as values under the definition's number and name (replacing that ID's rows wherever they are). At the end it restores the live scenario, the override and the calculation mode it found, sorts StoredOutputs, groups the blank scenario columns and refreshes the dashboard charts.
- **RecalculateNow**: full recalculation (timed), then the dashboard charts. The workbook ships with its values in manual calculation; **ToggleRecalculation** switches automatic calculation on or off (for every open workbook, as Excel does).
- **StoreBaseline**: replaces the stored baseline with the current scenario-1 results, after a confirmation.
- **StoreLiveScenario**: stores the live scenario as it stands, under an ID you choose (default: the next free ID from 100).
- **SolveETSLive**: ETS goal seek for the live scenario only. It fills the override prices and switches the override on.
- **ClearStoredScenarios**: deletes every stored scenario except the baseline.
- **SortStoredOutputs**: sorts StoredOutputs by code stem, then ID.
- **GroupBlankScenarios**: groups and collapses the scenario columns of ScenarioDefinition that have no name.
- **RefreshDashboard**: rebuilds the series of the dashboard charts from the scenarios with results in the chosen source (short names in the legend, baseline dashed grey, one colour per scenario slot) and hides the table rows of the others.
- **CheckBatchRun**: the first-run test (section 4). It reruns the batch, so the stored scenarios are recalculated by the application that runs it.

The ETS goal seek is legacy's damped log-space iteration, as in `ets_goalseek.py`. It starts from the override prices, or from the fast estimate if there are none. Each step is p × (proposed price / p) ^ alpha, mixed 0.3 with the previous iterate, with 5% smoothing. Alpha halves when the error grows (minimum 0.0625) and rises ×1.2 when the error more than halves (maximum 1). It stops when the worst |covered / cap − 1| is below 0.5%, or after 20 iterations.

#### 4. First run in Excel

The VBA project (written by `vba_project.py`) and the stored results were produced without Excel. They are tested in LibreOffice: the module loads, the macros reproduce the Python emulation, and CheckBatchRun passes. To confirm the same in Excel:

1. If the file was downloaded, unblock it first (file Properties > Unblock), or Excel opens it with macros disabled.
2. Open it and choose Enable Content.
3. Run **CheckBatchRun** (Alt+F8); it takes a minute or two. It checks the 12 lookups the macros rely on (sheets, rows by code, scenario columns, MTOutputs blocks); compares Excel's own recalculation of the baseline with the stored baseline (plain formulas only, so Excel and LibreOffice calculate it the same way); and reruns RunAllScenarios, ETS goal seek included, comparing every stored value with the value stored before.
4. MacroCheck shows **Result PASS** when no value differs by more than 1e-6 (relative). CHECK lists how many values differ; FAIL names the lookup that was not found.
5. If Excel cannot load the VBA project, or Alt+F8 lists no macros: remove the project if one is listed, import `CPATScenarios.bas` (Alt+F11 > File > Import), save as .xlsm and run CheckBatchRun again.

#### 5. Comparing and keeping results

- **Source and year.** On ScenarioCompare choose Results from (Stored or Live) and the year, then Recalculate now. Stored reads StoredOutputs (every stored scenario); Live reads MTOutputs (the scenario groups of Mitigation: the baseline and the live scenario, and any group added by copy-paste). The names SCVal, SCCode and SCYear choose the range with CHOOSE; every value is `INDEX(SCVal, MATCH(country.stem.ID, SCCode, 0), year column)`, so the order of the rows never matters.
- **Scenario slots.** Up to 10, in ScenarioDefinition order: ID, short name (the legend), name. A scenario with no result in the chosen source shows blank (key table) or #N/A (time series, hidden by a conditional format, a gap in the charts); the charts leave it out.
- **Key table.** Energy CO2 emissions, GHG emissions excluding LULUCF, revenue as a share of GDP, the GDP effect of the revenue use and the net welfare effect: level, difference from the baseline, and % difference for the two emission levels. The bar chart beside it shows the % difference of energy CO2 by scenario.
- **Time series.** Four tables (default: energy CO2, GHGs, revenue, GDP effect), scenarios down and years across, each with its line chart beside it. The title of each table is a dropdown of the indicator list at the bottom of the tab: every MTOutputs indicator except the price and Kaya indices.
- StoredOutputs holds values only, so results from other files can be pasted in as values under new IDs, as long as its column layout is kept (output code in column D).
- The baseline changes only when StoreBaseline is run.

#### 6. Limits

- The batch run calculates one policy scenario at a time. Further Mitigation scenario groups (copies of group 2) show on the dashboard under Live; the batch macros use the live scenario (group 2) only.
- MTOutputs (the legacy MTOutputs rows the prototype has and its own key outputs) defines what is stored: its Mitigation rows, each code once (about 830 per scenario); the distribution rows are live only. To store more, add rows to the MTOutputs blocks first.

## The distribution tab {#sec-distribution-tab}

*Source: [`excel_ai/mitigation/docs/methods/Distribution.md`](https://github.com/cpmodelai/cpat_ai/blob/main/excel_ai/mitigation/docs/methods/Distribution.md).*

The household incidence of a scenario in one analysis year, by decile. It follows legacy CPAT's sheet `Distribution` and its MTOutputs rows 911-1033, with legacy's bugs fixed.

- **Builder:** `build.py` (`build_distribution`, `build_distribution_data`, `build_mto_distribution`).
- **Data:** `extract_distn.py` writes `data/distn_*.csv`.
- **Independent check:** `distribution_ref.py`, a Python reference.
- **Legacy formulas:** the legacy sheet `Distribution`; the specification `other/more/CPAT_Distribution_Module_Pseudocode.docx`.

### 1. Layout (NORMS 1.1b)

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| Rows 1-12 | Row 1 holds 0 (shown as `Basket`) and the deciles 1-10. Rows 4-5: scenario name and number, formatted as Mitigation (frozen with rows 1-3). Row 6: position of the group. Rows 7-8: Mitigation column of the analysis year in group 1 and in this group. Row 9: statistic. Rows 10-11: survey code parts. Row 12: analysis year, the summary of section 0 (v0.4.8; row 10 before). |
| Roll-up (v0.4.8, NORMS 2.5) | One row group per section: the band and, below the hidden rows, the summary row (last in its section) and one blank row stay visible. Summaries, all overall: 0 analysis year, 1 options check, 2 revenue, 3 average indirect price change of the consumption categories (budget-share weighted), 4 average price factor of the household fuels (budget-share weighted), 5 energy budget share (fuels and biomass), 6 total effect, 7 total consumption, 8 recycling gain, 9 net effect after recycling. Sections 6-9 list urban and rural first, overall last. Columns C:G and I:K are one column group each, rolled up, as Mitigation; zoom 75. |
| Columns | A variable, B item, C sample (`ove`, `urb`, `rur`), D-E parameters (data variable, sample label), H description, I unit, J source (legacy rows). Per group: code column, basket, deciles 1-10, spacer (13 columns, from K; v0.4.8: deciles 9 wide; totals in local currency shown in bn and population in m, values unchanged). |
| Groups | 1 = scenario 1 (levels; effects 0), 2 = the policy scenario, 3 = the LAMBDA test group (runs group 2's scenario and reads Mitigation's LAMBDA group). Pasting group 2 to the right adds scenarios 3-6 (NORMS 3e, scenario capacity). |
| Row kinds | Settings and one-value rows: the value in the basket column, repeated across the deciles (so every cell refers to its own column). Decile rows: one formula across basket and deciles. Decile-only rows (recycling): the basket column is blank. |
| Codes | `iso.distn.<variable>[.<item>][.dec.<sample>].<scenario>`. MTOutputs (v1.0.4) reads them in each scenario block (deciles 1-10 in K:T); its column F gives the legacy code (without the scenario suffix, as legacy). |

### 2. Chain (sections of the sheet)

| Section | Formula | Legacy |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Settings | The 23 ScenarioDefinition distribution settings of the group's scenario (rows 197-205, 304-319). Derived: infrastructure-access variable, ASPIRE program, most-used cooking fuel. A support check names any option v0.4.4 does not model. | B.I |
| 2 Inputs | **Household price change by fuel:** residential after-tax price `atp.<f>.res` (electricity: retail price `rp.ecy.res`) / scenario 1 - 1. **Economy-wide change:** `rpn` (coal and gas: industry; oil products: all sectors; electricity: `rp.ecy.ind`). **Scenario-1 base-year spending:** `pav.sp`. **Macro inputs:** GDP (LCU), population, new-policy revenue (`rnew` x `xr`). | B.II-B.III, C.I 528-556, I152-I237 |
| 3 Indirect prices | Category price change = Σ_f Lcat(c,f) x g_f. Lcat is the household-demand weighted Leontief coefficient (IO_GTAP table). g_f = R_f / T_f, with R_f = Σ spending x price change of the fuel group and T_f = total embedded plus own use. | C.I 496-736 |
| 4 Price factors | dp x (1 + dp)^ε (HH_Elast, decile-specific; PEDs). The exempt cooking fuel is 0 for the bottom deciles. | C.II 801-825 |
| 5 Budget shares | HHSurvey by sample, statistic (row 9) and decile. | C.III-C.IV |
| 6 Effects | Effect = -price factor x budget share x loss scale (% of consumption, loss negative). Loss scale = behavioural factor (InferredDist: revenue / implied revenue) + DWLTri x (1 - factor) if DWLs. | C.V-C.VII, D.II |
| 7 Rebasing | Population = survey population x population / survey population. Per-capita consumption = survey value x national consumption / (survey basket x population). National consumption = GDP x consumption share (WDI, latest year). | C.VIII |
| 8 Recycling | **PIT** (personal allowance, proportional, targeted exemption). **Targeted cash transfer** (bottom percentile, coverage, leakage). **Public investment** (people without access). **Current spending** (ASPIRE quintiles). All per capita, then in % of each sample's consumption. | C.X-C.XI |
| 9 Net, compensation, Gini | Net effect = effect + recycling. Compensation share = loss x consumption / Σ. Gini = 1 - SUMPRODUCT(consumption, DGiniW) / SUM(consumption), base, after the price effects and after recycling. | C.IX, C.XII, D.V |

Two identities let the sheet stay short:

1. **Indirect prices (ScaleGTAP = Yes, legacy default).**
   - Legacy rescales each GTAP sector's raw price change by k(s) = Σ_f σ(f,s) R_f / Σ_f Emb(f,s) dp(f,s).
   - With Emb(f,s) = Y_s L(f,s) and σ(f,s) = Emb(f,s) / T_f, the sector's adjusted change is Σ_f L(f,s) R_f / T_f. The sector-specific fuel prices cancel.
   - Checked on legacy's cache: all 59 sectors to 4e-16, and the 14 categories to 3e-6 (legacy prints 6 digits).
   - ScaleGTAP = No uses g_f = R_f / spending_f, i.e. the economy-wide price change. Legacy instead uses the price change of each GTAP sector's CPAT sector; that simplification is recorded.
2. **Gini.**
   - Legacy fits L(x) = a x² + b x to the cumulative decile shares (LINEST, no intercept) and takes Gini = (5 - area) / 5.
   - The fit is linear in L, so Gini = 1 - Σ_j s_j W_j with fixed weights W_j (DistMapping, name DGiniW; `distribution_ref.gini_weights`).
   - Replicated as an issue: the fitted curve, not the trapezoid rule.

### 3. Bugs fixed (not replicated; NORMS 0)

| Legacy | Bug | v0.4.4 |
|---|---|---|
| R2562:Z2562 | The targeted share of a decile is capped at 10 points, not its population share: 105.6% of decile 2 receives the transfer. | Capped at the decile's population share. |
| C.V/C.VI basket (e.g. Q1607) | The basket uses decile 1's elasticity adjustment and exemption test. | The basket uses the basket elasticity and is never exempt. |
| Q2633 | Current spending tests the ASPIRE flag of the targeted transfer (I213), not of current spending (I214). | No flag: the ASPIRE program of the chosen type, 0 if absent. |
| 2701-2707 | Public investment and current spending are 0 when the transfer coverage or percentile is 0. | Independent of the transfer settings. |
| Q2749 | The targeted exemption is capped by all carbon-pricing revenue (I154), not the PIT share (I163); urban and rural values are not per capita. | Capped by the PIT revenue; per capita in every sample. |
| Q3259, Q3263 | The urban and rural compensation shares divide by overall consumption weights (they sum to 52 and 47). | Each sample's own weights: each sums to 100. |
| 859-883 | Deadweight loss is a price fraction subtracted from a % of consumption. | DWLTri x (1 - factor) x the effect (same units). |
| MTOutputs 1001-1002 | dist.year and dist.stat read ScenarioDefinition column D (0 in dashboard mode). | The analysis year and statistic of the group. |

The bug fixes change Egypt's legacy numbers only a little: the targeted transfer in deciles 1-4 moves by up to 0.13 points of consumption, and the Gini change with recycling by 0.0006 points. The urban and rural compensation shares move most, because each now sums to 100.

### 4. Issues replicated (tracked)

- **Spending year:** fuel spending in the base year (legacy: first calculation year), with analysis-year price changes.
- **Deflator:** the GTAP values are converted with the local GDP deflator (legacy I244).
- **Elasticities:** always overall, mean (the data have no other).
- **Recycled amounts:** per capita from the overall sample, applied to urban and rural consumption.
- **Lorenz-fit Gini** (section 2).
- **Revenue:** revenue from new policies (`rnew`) stands for legacy's carbon-pricing revenue (carbon tax, VAT on it, auctioned ETS).

### 5. Options and outputs added in v0.6.0 (every legacy option now modelled)

- **Targeted transfer** (section 8): one formula for the three legacy modes. Weight per decile w = 1 (Cash), the share
  below the poverty line (TargetBelow, with Cash only; HHSurvey `pct_belowpl_*` x 10, at most 100%, mean as legacy) or
  the ASPIRE benefit of the TransferType program for the decile's quintile. Transfer per capita = revenue x w x share
  receiving / Σ w x share receiving x population, so the payout equals the revenue (legacy pays 125-129% on the ASPIRE
  path, L147). A program without data for the country falls back to cash and the settings check says so (legacy drops
  the transfer, L148). Median statistic: the transfer reaches only deciles where more than half receive (legacy row 2685;
  the money not paid is not redistributed, as legacy); public investment and current spending are not flagged (L150).
  Switch tests (Egypt): Cash Transfers program 1, 1, 0.691, 0.691, 0.047 of decile 1; poverty line 6.85: 1, 1, 1,
  0.507, 0.003; as the legacy formulas with the fixes applied to legacy's cached inputs.
- **Outputs for charts** (section 10, legacy D.I-D.V): decile labels (QuantilesLCU: consumption brackets in real local
  currency of the analysis year, L157-L158), budget shares by group, urban and rural direct and indirect effects by item,
  per-capita (local currency) budgets, effects and net effect, Lorenz curves (baseline as legacy: 4.016, 9.045, 16.106),
  cumulative compensation, the 25th and 75th percentile households (L155-L156), Gini change in points.
- **Production sectors** (section 11, legacy D.VI): input-cost price change of each GTAP sector (Leontief
  coefficients x fuel-group factors, the identity of section 2), output price after pass-through (PassthroughDist;
  coefficients by CPAT sector, L163), rank and top 20 (ties broken, L162), 14 CPAT sectors (chemicals and power added, L161)
  with demand and output shares and weighted prices; MTOutputs `ppic`, `ppici`, `outpriin` by sector code (L164).
  Data: `data/distn_gtapmap.csv` (legacy Mapping F/R/H), `data/distn_passthrough.csv` (legacy Distribution I470:I486).
- **Charts** (sheet Charts, below the mitigation charts): the legacy Dashboard distribution charts from group 2.

### 6. Checks

- **Python reference:** fed with legacy's cached Egypt inputs, it reproduces legacy's outputs to the precision of the cache (`python distribution_ref.py`): effects, recycling, net effect and compensation to 4e-4, Gini changes to 7e-6.
- **Quick check:**
  - group 2 of the sheet equals the reference fed with the sheet's own inputs;
  - the LAMBDA group equals group 2;
  - no error values;
  - scenario numbers align with Mitigation group by group.
- **Paste test** (`check_paste.py`): Distribution groups 4-7 are pasted with Mitigation's.

## Data tabs {#sec-data-tabs}

*Source: [`excel_ai/mitigation/docs/methods/Data_tabs.md`](https://github.com/cpmodelai/cpat_ai/blob/main/excel_ai/mitigation/docs/methods/Data_tabs.md).*

User request (2026-10-17): align the data tabs with legacy CPAT (grouped by module, legacy order, legacy names and
content where possible, without undoing principled decisions); check that the model would work with the full
all-country data; put every Egypt-only table alone on its tab or at the bottom; check how far the legacy data tables
can be copied in. Then (same day): align more fully, going with the recommendations. The norm is NORMS.md 1.5.

### Summary

- **Order.** The data tabs sit under the legacy dividers in legacy order: `DATA_MITIGATION->>`, `DATA_DISTN->>`,
  `DATA_TRAN->>`, `DATA_OUTPUT->>`; tabs without a legacy data tab come last under `DATA_OTHER->>` (BaselineCO2 only).
- **Copy-in rules (NORMS 1.5).**
  - **L, a single legacy table:** the table itself, unchanged (same columns, column letters and codes; header row 3,
    data from A4; a key formula column right of the table where legacy has no unique key). Paste the legacy data rows
    at A4. 17 tabs: Balances, EnergyCons, CH4Inputs, UNPop, OilProductShares (v0.4.12), WEO, EF_GHG, SCC, EF_PM,
    IO_GTAP, HHSurvey, HH_Elast, ASPIRE, WHOCooking, GDPRatios, Transport1, Transport2.
  - **A, a legacy tab with several tables:** kept at its legacy cell addresses from row 3 (rows 1-2: source line and
    title bar). Paste the legacy tab from row 3. 10 tabs: Countries, Elasticities, ETS+LTS, Multipliers, Prices_int,
    ECP, Transport3 (stored results, rows 5+) and, since v0.4.7, Power, CoC and GHGs (the inventory and, rows
    1201-1388, the 2023-2024 emission shocks of the power model).
  - **L*, Prices_dom:** legacy header rows and codes; paste legacy rows 4 onwards at A1.
- **Country selection is a data step (NORMS 1.5, rule 2c).** What legacy Mitigation computes from these tabs for the
  selected country sits in blocks of the Inputs tab, by formula, under the keys the model already used:
  - Inputs_ela: elasticities (the country's column of Elasticities, as legacy column G);
  - Inputs_mult: multipliers (median ± standard deviation by group, instrument and lag);
  - Inputs_macro: GDP growth and levels, deflators, exchange rate (WEO series with legacy's extension past the last data
    year, rows 417-467) and the energy trade balance and share traded (rows 741-743, from Balances);
  - Inputs_pint: international price series by source (rows 633-695);
  - Inputs_ecp: existing carbon pricing (rows 1675-1764; v0.4.12: carbon tax with single and fuel rates, national ETS and
    EU ETS, each code looked up in its own legacy block of ECP, coverage by data year, and two tables by ECP sector and
    fuel: carbon tax and ETS in \$/tCO2);
  - Inputs_ef: CO2 emission factors (rows 980-1011);
  - Inputs_nc (v0.9.0): non-CO2 combustion emission factors of local pollutants and CH4 by legacy EF code (rows
    1052-1663: country, else World Bank region, else world, from the all-country EF_PM; other energy the maximum
    across the other subsectors);
  - v0.4.7, power (legacy section 4, rows 2954-4300): Inputs_pset (the power settings of ScenarioDefinition scenario 1 and derived
    values, each a defined name Ps...), Inputs_ptech (one row per generation type, the former PowerTech: country, else
    world parameters, efficiency and generation from Balances, WACC from CoC, capacity factors), Inputs_ppath (year
    paths, the former PowerPaths: capex time factors, storage, income factor, fuel price shocks, prices) and
    Inputs_ppar (parameters, the former PowerParams). The chains are mapped in chapter Power.
  The Egypt values reproduce legacy's cached values (macro series to 1e-15; power data to 1e-12), apart from one legacy
  bug fixed (L51: the coal trade balance was valued at the oil price) and one stale value in legacy's stored run (I38:
  the wind and solar capex time factors for 2039-2041 differ from the legacy Power cells they reference; the prototype
  follows the Power tab).
- **Proprietary tables.** The public legacy file (`CPAT 1.0pre_456_NoPropData.xlsb`) holds Egypt only in Balances,
  EnergyCons (empty), Prices_dom, EF_PM, IO_GTAP, HHSurvey, ASPIRE, WHOCooking, CalVal and Tran_Scatter. The model
  uses the first eight; all eight paste in directly.
- **All-country test: PASS.** `check_allcountry.py` clones every Egypt row of every single-table tab under a dummy
  country (XEG) at the bottom of its table, renames Egypt's codes to XEG in place on the tabs kept at legacy addresses,
  selects XEG and recalculates: no error values, every output of Mitigation and Distribution identical to Egypt's.
- **No table from legacy's cached Egypt run is left (v0.4.7).** The former PowerTech, PowerPaths and PowerParams are
  computed from the legacy tabs on Inputs. BaselineCO2 (the scenario-1 CO2 the calibration uses) is derived by the
  build.
- **Legacy bugs in the power data: all fixed (v0.4.10, NORMS 0; v0.4.7 still copied them):** L52 every generation type
  takes the country parameters where they exist (Egypt: solar fixed O&M 11.831 instead of 15 \$/kW/y); L53 the actual
  capacity factor of the base year (installed capacity, Power rows 358-1635) is used inside the CFOverride bounds (Egypt:
  gas 0.385, wind 0.436, solar 0.347, hydro 0.592; base-year gas capacity 52 GW instead of 35); L54 hydro invests from
  the base year only when its generation share is above 50% (Egypt: from 2030); L55 the country rows are looked up in
  the country block first (China, Japan, Korea); L56 countries without CoC risk data take the default WACC, flagged.
- Balances, EnergyCons, EF_PM, IO_GTAP, HHSurvey, HH_Elast, ASPIRE, WHOCooking and GDPRatios became legacy tables
  (v0.4.5). Then GHGs, CH4Inputs, UNPop, EF_GHG, SCC, Transport1 and Transport2 followed. The tables come
  from `extract_legacy_tables.py`, which writes `legacy_<Tab>.csv` verbatim from the legacy file (today into the legacy-form cache
  `.buildcache/legacy_csv/<edition>/`, saved to `data/<edition>/tidy/` by `data/scripts/legacy_csv.py`).
- Base-year fuel use and power demand now come from Balances through legacy's flow mapping (Mapping columns J-M), as
  legacy does with BalancesOrConsumption = Balances; the old PowerDemand tab was dropped.
- CO2 emission factors: the legacy EF_GHG table replaces the Egypt factors copied from legacy's run. The selection of
  legacy Mitigation rows 980-1011 is now a data step on Inputs, and it reproduces the Egypt factors exactly:
  - the country's code, else its World Bank region, else the world;
  - LPG and kerosene in power, and coal, LPG, kerosene and other oil products in road, take the row legacy points to;
  - jet fuel uses the IEA factor (EFJetIEA);
  - biomass is zero.
- GHGs: the legacy table adds Zimbabwe 2021 (legacy row 947). The previous extract stopped at row 946.
- All named ranges over data tables reach the capacity of the full legacy tables, with margin.
- v0.4.6: Countries, Elasticities, ETS+LTS, Multipliers, Prices_int, ECP and Transport3 became legacy tabs at legacy
  addresses (`legacy_<Tab>_cells.csv` in the legacy-form cache), WEO the legacy table; the selections legacy makes for the country became
  the Inputs blocks above; the GHG inventory year and every other lookup are unchanged.
- v0.4.6 results against v0.4.5: unchanged except the coal trade balance (L51 fixed; external balance rows xtb, about
  0.6 bn USD a year for Egypt) and the base-year lagged GDP growth of the road model (trgdl, 2022: the WEO 2021 growth
  3.25 % instead of 0, transport bug B2 now fixed, as the builder intended; the old WEO copy had no 2021 growth).
- v0.4.7: Power, CoC and GHGs became legacy tabs at legacy addresses; the power data of the country (the former tabs
  PowerTech, PowerPaths and PowerParams, copied from legacy's Egypt run) became the Inputs power blocks, formulas only
  (country, else world parameters; efficiency and generation from Balances; WACC from CoC; capex time factors, storage,
  income factor, emission shocks; settings from ScenarioDefinition scenario 1). The values reproduce the former tables, except
  the wind and solar capex time factors for 2039-2041 (I94). Effect on Egypt's results: none before 2039; from 2039
  new capacity and investment of solar, wind and gas, then power fuel use and emissions (525 output codes; largest:
  new solar investment in the baseline, by up to 149 MW a year).
- Dropped in v0.4.7: PowerTech, PowerPaths, PowerParams (now Inputs blocks from Power, CoC, Balances, WEO, GHGs).
- v0.4.12: OilProductShares (legacy table, all countries; household share of diesel, kerosene, LPG and gasoline, and
  their road shares) after UNPop, as legacy. Inputs_prices multiplies the VAT rate of gasoline, diesel, LPG and
  kerosene by the household share, as legacy rows 797-816 (LD5, issue I39). Settings rows 46-51: the methane fee
  switches per source of legacy Manual inputs J196-J200 (LD46; since v0.5.2 on sheet Manual inputs, shown on Settings). Inputs columns efxs:eff (v0.9.0: removed, legacy 465 factors; nearest GAINS factors, bug
  L59) and ecpk, xcp0 (existing carbon pricing), which replace ctc and etc.

### Manual inputs: the second input source, at the legacy addresses

Sheet `Manual inputs` (tab group INPUTS->>, after ScenarioDefinition) is the whole legacy tab of that name, rows 3-378 at their
legacy cell addresses (rows 1-2: source line and title bar), so the legacy tab pasted from row 3 replaces it. The cells
come from `legacy_ManualInputs_cells.csv` in the legacy-form cache (`extract_legacy_tables.py manual`): legacy values typed, light
green on the input cells. Legacy formulas within the sheet are kept (unit labels, the SCC path, the memo rows, the
residual of the PM2.5 apportionment); formulas that read other legacy tabs are replaced by the prototype equivalent (country
name and code, ScenarioDefinition scenario 1, the Elasticities tab) or typed as their legacy default value, and the note on the
block's title row (column J) says which. ScenarioDefinition stays the main input sheet (NORMS 4).
